title: New Governor, Old Problem: Koja Confronts US Base-Related Crimes in Okinawa
gist: LDP-backed Koja Genta ousted Denny Tamaki as Okinawa governor in September 2026, seen as friendlier to US bases and the Futenma-to-Henoko relocation, but quickly faced a US base-related crime when he protested a woman's alleged murder by a US Marine.

insights.claim: Koja Genta, the LDP's preferred candidate, ousted incumbent Okinawa Governor Denny Tamaki in the September 2026 election, becoming the first LDP-backed winner since Hirokazu Nakaima in 2006.
insights.speaker: Charmaine N. Willis
insights.so_what: Removes a long-standing local political obstacle to US base plans in Okinawa.
insights.quote: Koja became the first LDP-backed candidate to win the position since Hirokazu Nakaima in 2006.

insights.claim: Tamaki and his predecessor Onaga Takeshi vocally opposed expanding the US Marine Corps' Camp Schwab in Henoko and criticized Okinawa's excessive base burden relative to other Japanese prefectures.
insights.speaker: Charmaine N. Willis
insights.so_what: Context for why the governor change matters for alliance basing.

insights.claim: Tokyo's LDP-led government views Governor Koja as more favorable to US bases, specifically completing the relocation of Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan to Camp Schwab.
insights.speaker: Charmaine N. Willis
insights.so_what: Could accelerate the long-delayed Futenma relocation and related construction.

insights.claim: On October 7, 2026, Governor Koja lodged a written protest with Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae and Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara Minou over the murder of a woman allegedly by a US Marine.
insights.speaker: Charmaine N. Willis
insights.so_what: Base-related crimes can quickly reignite Okinawan opposition even under a pro-base governor.
insights.quote: lodges a written protest over the murder of a woman, allegedly by a U.S. Marine

insights.claim: The author frames US base-related crime as an 'old problem' that confronts even a base-friendly new Okinawa governor, implying the structural friction over US forces persists regardless of who governs.
insights.speaker: Charmaine N. Willis
insights.so_what: Political alignment alone may not de-risk US-Japan basing frictions.
